content: In a proper type theoretic setting with proof relevance included we may be able to perform searches over the proof structure to help all mathematicians that are in the situation asking themselves "I used that proof technique somewhere in my wide catalog of theorems, I wonder where that was?" Is there any tooling in Lean or Mathlib to allow for such pattern matching if the proof is included as data attached to a (type universe and above level) type or structured in some proof relevant way?

I'm not aware of such tools but most likely they would use metaprogramming and thus "proof irrelevance" really does not matter for building such tools.

For understanding your question, I think it would be very helpful if you could mention a simple concrete example for "a technique which you'd like to be able to search for"

I guess you could think of any case out there where a mathematician tells you "this proof uses a novel technique" or a "familiar technique" as a way of referring recognizing patterns in proofs or such techniques would not be comparable on the first place. But I guess brought down to Lean proofs this would be recognizing a sequence of tactics chained in a particular way with similarities in the goals and likely proof states to be recognized and extracted as well. Note however I am not referring to identical goals which would of course end up as a refactored theorem.
